explanation:
Looking at the three demonstrations, the only change is that colour 2 cells get added around certain objects; nothing else moves. Where exactly do the 2s go? In pair 3 the small 2×2 block at [4,4]–[5,5] receives 2s at (3,4),(3,5),(4,3),(4,6),(5,3),(5,6),(6,4),(6,5): for each of the four corner cells of the block, the two cells just outside it orthogonally (one above/below, one left/right). The big 8×8 ring gets the same treatment at its corners: (0,1),(1,0) around corner (1,1), and so on, up to (8,9),(9,8) around corner (8,8). Pairs 1 and 2 follow the identical pattern around the 4×4 ring and the 3×3 ring: eight 2s, two "shoulders" per corner.

Which objects are decorated? Decorated: 4×4 ring, 3×3 ring, 8×8 ring, 2×2 block. Not decorated: the 2×4 solid rectangle (pair 1), the 1×3 and 3×1 lines (pair 2), the single pixels (pair 1). The decorated objects are exactly those whose bounding box is a square with side at least 2 (single pixels are squares but are not marked, and nothing that is wider than tall or vice versa is marked). Whether the square is hollow or solid does not matter (8×8 hollow ring and 2×2 solid block both count).

So the rule: for every non-background object whose bounding box is a square of side ≥ 2, paint colour 2 on the two orthogonal outside neighbours of each of its four corner cells (skipping any that would fall outside the grid). Note the 2×2 block's marks in pair 3 land inside the larger ring — they just go on background cells wherever they are.

On the test input there are two 3×3 hollow squares (at [1,1]–[3,3] and [5,5]–[7,7]), two 2×2 solid blocks (at [1,6]–[2,7] and [6,1]–[7,2]) and an 8-long horizontal line in row 9. The line has a non-square bounding box, so it stays untouched; each of the other four objects gets eight red shoulder cells around its corners. I emit a canvas after decorating each qualifying object.
